title: Palliative Care Access And Continuity Gaps In Low- And Middle-Income Countries
summary: Build a verified measurement layer for palliative-care need, referral, service delivery, medicine access, caregiver support, and continuity across primary, community, home, and specialist care in low- and middle-income countries.
why_it_matters: A Ministry of Health universal-health-coverage director, national medicines regulator, or health funder must decide whether to finance palliative care in the primary-care benefits package, district and home services, workforce training, and an essential-medicine supply line. WHO's 2020 fact sheet estimates that 56.8 million people need palliative care each year and that about 14% receive it; the same source reports that only 40% of 194 Member States said services reached at least half of patients in need in a 2019 survey (evidence: who-palliative-care-burden-access-2020). WHO has since published actionable indicators, but countries still need a comparable, decision-ready cascade that separates population need from referral, contact, symptom support, caregiver support, medicine availability, and continuity (evidence: who-palliative-care-actionable-indicators-2021). Verified country or district evidence could change a real benefits-package, workforce, service-location, or procurement allocation; it must not be converted into a clinical-effect or opioid-policy recommendation without domain, red-team, field-reality, and independent replication review.

success_metrics.target: Every palliative-care need estimate records its age, diagnosis or serious-health-related-suffering definition, reference year, population frame, numerator, denominator, uncertainty, and missingness; terminal-care counts are not silently substituted for all need.
success_metrics.validation_method: A replicator reconstructs the denominator from the cited source methods and blocks estimates whose definition, grain, or reference year is not recoverable.

success_metrics.target: Every setting separates policy and financing, service availability, referral, first contact, ongoing symptom support, caregiver support, transfer, and documented closure or loss to follow-up.
success_metrics.validation_method: A domain reviewer traces each cascade field to a source measure and records where the source observes only capacity, not patient-level access or continuity.

success_metrics.target: Morphine or other medicine indicators distinguish legal authorization, procurement, facility-day availability, stock continuity, affordability, dispensing, and clinically appropriate use; consumption is never treated as a complete palliative-care coverage measure.
success_metrics.validation_method: A medicines-access reviewer reruns the indicator definitions and checks availability, affordability, consumption, and service records as separate measurement families.

success_metrics.target: Any future field artifact records consent, patient-defined goals, symptom or function measures, caregiver burden, equity, complaints, and attrition without claiming mortality or hospitalization effects.
success_metrics.validation_method: A field-reality and red-team review checks that outcome fields are collected with appropriate consent and that operational contact is not misreported as clinical benefit.

success_metrics.target: No resource-allocation, clinical, controlled-medicine, or service-expansion recommendation advances beyond measurement framing without the required domain, red-team, field-reality, and replication reviews.
success_metrics.validation_method: Review records and an independent replication are checked before any country-facing or operational output is published.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, palliative-care and health-systems domain review, red-team review for controlled-medicine and clinical overreach, field-reality review for country allocation use, and independent replication before any quantitative or operational recommendation.
